source: Udrescu, Tegmark (2020) AI Feynman: a physics-inspired method for symbolic regression
finding: Recursive search plus neural net fit plus physics tricks (symmetry, separability, dimensional analysis) solved all 100 Feynman equations. Eureqa solved 71.
numbers: 100/100 vs 71/100 for Eureqa. Harder physics set: success rate 15% to 90%.
limits: Noise-free data; equations chosen by the authors; later benchmark shows brittleness (b03).
agent_relevance: Heuristics that exploit problem structure (split into sub-problems) beat brute search; supports a subgoal library.

source: Udrescu et al. (2020) AI Feynman 2.0: Pareto-optimal symbolic regression
finding: Added a Pareto front over accuracy and complexity, generalized symmetry finding, and hypothesis tests. Much more robust to noise.
numbers: 73 of 100 Feynman problems solved with noise sd 0.1 (r=-1). Noise robustness 1-3 orders of magnitude better than v1. Given 2 h, v1 solved 5 of the new modular mysteries, v2 solved all 12 plus 4 of the 17 old failures.
quote: typically being orders of magnitude more robust toward noise and bad data
limits: Authors' own benchmark; new test set chosen by authors before testing.
agent_relevance: Rank hypotheses by fit and simplicity together, not fit alone (links to MDL-style guardrails).

source: La Cava et al. (2021) Contemporary symbolic regression methods and their relative performance (SRBench)
finding: Independent large benchmark: 14 symbolic regression methods and 7 ML methods on 252 problems. Tests the claims of AI Feynman and others under noise.
numbers: Zero noise ground truth: AIFeynman exact solution 53% of the time, next best GP-GOMEA 27%. Above noise 0.01, DSR, gplearn, AFP_FE and AFP recover exact solutions more often. On Strogatz data few significant differences among top 10. Best on real-world data: Operon, yet it finds few exact formulas.
quote: AIFeynman may be brittle in application to real-world and/or noisy data
limits: Fixed time budgets; ground truth only for known physics equations and ODE systems.
agent_relevance: Do not trust a headline from one method. Exact-law recovery and predictive fit are different goals; check both.

source: Cranmer (2023) Interpretable machine learning for science with PySR and SymbolicRegression.jl (EmpiricalBench)
finding: EmpiricalBench: 9 historical empirical laws (Hubble, Kepler, Newton, Planck, Leavitt, Schechter, Bode, ideal gas, Rydberg), 5 trials per method. Classic untrained heuristic searchers (PySR, Operon, DSR, QLattice) all out-performed the pretrained SR-Transformer; PySR recovered the most.
numbers: 9 laws x 5 trials x 6 algorithms. PySR got several laws 5/5; EQL, QLattice and SR-Transformer were mostly 0/5. Exact per-cell counts are garbled in the PDF text, so not recorded.
limits: Scored by eye because sympy equality checks failed. Author wrote PySR (conflict of interest). The text also describes BACON and Fahrenheit as early heuristic search over expression trees.
agent_relevance: A cheap heuristic search with a complexity penalty rivals a heavy learned model: keep generate-and-test with a simplicity bias.

source: Shojaee et al. (2024) LLM-SR: scientific equation discovery via programming with LLMs
finding: LLM proposes equation skeletons as programs, an optimizer fits constants, an evolutionary buffer keeps the best. Beat PySR and uDSR using 2.5K iterations vs 2M+ for baselines. Gap is largest out of domain.
numbers: E. coli growth OOD NMSE about 0.0037 vs above 1 for other methods. Ablation (Oscillation 2, GPT-3.5): no iterative refinement NMSE 1.01e-1 ID and 1.81e-1 OOD; no skeleton plus optimizer 3.78e-1 ID and 3.75e-1 OOD; removing the natural-language prior also hurt a lot; single-line expressions hurt less.
limits: Four benchmarks built by the authors; GPT-3.5 and Mixtral backbones only. Perplexity test suggests the LLM recites known Feynman equations.
agent_relevance: Each component maps to our loop: prior knowledge, generate, fit, keep best. Dropping the test-and-refine loop costs most.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) LLM-SRBench: a new benchmark for scientific equation discovery with LLMs
finding: 239 problems built to block memorisation (LSR-Transform: common laws rewritten; LSR-Synth: synthetic). Best system reaches only 31.5% symbolic accuracy. Feynman problems show sharp error drops, a memorisation sign.
numbers: Best symbolic accuracy 31.5%. Direct prompting about 2-7% SA on Transform. LaSR with Llama-3.1-8B: 45.9% Acc0.1 on Transform. LLM-SR with GPT-4o-mini about 31% SA on Transform. Methods: direct prompt, SGA, LaSR, LLM-SR; backbones Llama-3.1-8B, GPT-3.5, GPT-4o-mini.
limits: Small backbones, no frontier reasoning models. Ranking flips by domain: LaSR better symbolic accuracy in material science, LLM-SR better numeric fit. Symbolic accuracy correlates positively with OOD accuracy.
agent_relevance: Real discovery gain is small once recall is blocked. Test our agent on disguised problems, not textbook ones.

source: Majumder et al. (2024) DiscoveryBench: towards data-driven discovery with LLMs
finding: 264 real tasks from papers in 6 domains plus 903 synthetic tasks. Best agent scores 25%. Domain knowledge helps: archaeology tasks go from 9.9% to 17.5% when expert hints are added (DataVoyager, GPT-4p).
numbers: Best 25%. By domain: biology 0%, engineering 7%, economics 25%, sociology 23%. Replicating a paper workflow took up to 90 person-hours and 30% did not reproduce.
limits: Facet-based scoring uses an LLM judge; agents are from 2024.
agent_relevance: Failures sit in workflow steps, not only the final answer. Add domain priors early.

source: Chen et al. (2024) ScienceAgentBench: language agents for data-driven scientific discovery
finding: 102 tasks from 44 papers in four fields, validated by 9 experts. Best agent with 3 attempts solves 32.4% alone and 34.3% with expert knowledge. OpenAI o1-preview reaches 42.2% at over 10 times the cost.
numbers: Claude-3.5-Sonnet with self-debug 34.3% (with expert knowledge). Self-debug solved 10.8% more tasks than OpenHands CodeAct. Claude-3.5-Sonnet 16.7% without knowledge under another setting (as reported in the text).
limits: Single-file Python tasks; not end-to-end science.
agent_relevance: Self-debug (run, see error, repair) is a proven lever, matching a generate-test-repair operator. Extra compute helps but is costly.

source: Novikov et al. (2025) AlphaEvolve: a coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
finding: LLM-driven evolutionary search over programs with automatic evaluators. On over 50 math constructions it matched the best known on 75% and beat them on 20%. Found a 4x4 complex matrix multiply with 48 scalar multiplications, first gain over Strassen in 56 years.
numbers: 50+ problems: 75% matched, 20% improved. Ablations on tensor decomposition and kissing number test no-evolution, no-context-in-prompt and smaller-LLM variants; the full system is better and larger LLMs do better.
limits: Needs a fast machine-checkable score. White paper from the system's makers.
agent_relevance: Strongest case for generate and test with a trustworthy evaluator. Without one, expect weaker results.

source: Lu et al. (2024) The AI Scientist: towards fully automated open-ended scientific discovery
finding: End-to-end LLM system: idea, code, experiments, paper, automated review. Claims under 15 dollars per paper and papers above a top-conference acceptance threshold as judged by its own automated reviewer.
numbers: Under 15 dollars per paper; 3 ML subfields (diffusion, language modeling, learning dynamics).
limits: Success judged by an LLM reviewer built by the same authors; uses human code templates. Independent audits find serious flaws (b11, b12).
agent_relevance: Self-grading is the weak point. Use external checks.

source: Beel et al. (2025) Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist for autonomous research
finding: Independent test of AI Scientist. 5 of 12 experiments (42%) failed from coding errors. Known ideas such as micro-batching for SGD were marked novel. Median 5 citations per paper; only 5 of 34 citations from 2020 or later. Code changed only 8% per iteration.
numbers: Cost 6 to 15 dollars and 3.5 hours of human time per paper.
quote: an unmotivated undergraduate student rushing to meet a deadline
limits: Few runs; one evaluator group.
agent_relevance: Novelty checks by keyword search are unreliable; build a real prior-art check and validate execution.

source: Luo, Kasirzadeh, Shah (2025) The more you automate, the less you see: hidden pitfalls of AI scientist systems
finding: Controlled tests of two open AI scientist systems for four flaws: bad benchmark choice, data leakage, metric misuse, post-hoc selection. Agent Laboratory chose the first four listed benchmarks in 82.4% of 945 runs regardless of difficulty. Trace logs and code catch flaws far better than the paper alone.
numbers: 82.4% of 945 successful runs (with SOTA reference) chose the first four benchmarks; 79.6% in the other setting.
limits: Only two systems; ML research domain.
agent_relevance: Keep full traces; guard against position bias and post-hoc selection.

source: Si, Hashimoto, Yang (2024) Can LLMs generate novel research ideas? A large-scale human study with 100+ NLP researchers
finding: Blind review of 49 human ideas vs 49 LLM-agent ideas by 79 experts. LLM ideas rated more novel, slightly weaker on feasibility. Generation lacks diversity: about 5% of seed ideas survive deduplication at cosine 0.8. LLMs are poor judges of ideas.
numbers: Novelty 5.64 (AI) vs 4.84 (human) on a 1-10 scale, p<0.05; 79 reviewers from 32 institutions; N=49 ideas per condition.
limits: Idea-only judgment with no execution; novelty is subjective.
agent_relevance: Dedup and diversity control needed in the hypothesis generator; do not let the model rank its own ideas.

source: Si, Hashimoto, Yang (2025) The ideation-execution gap: execution outcomes of LLM-generated versus human research ideas
finding: Follow-up: 43 experts each spent over 100 hours executing randomly assigned human or LLM ideas. After execution LLM-idea scores fell much more than human ones and the ranking flipped on many metrics. The early novelty edge did not survive execution.
numbers: Score change after execution: human novelty -0.010, excitement +0.078, effectiveness -0.052; LLM ideas -1.049, -1.760, -1.879 (1-10 scale); p<0.05 on all four metrics.
limits: N=43 projects, modest; NLP only; executors were humans, not agents.
agent_relevance: Test hypotheses by running them before trusting them; ideation scores overstate quality.

source: Yamada et al. (2025) The AI Scientist-v2: workshop-level automated scientific discovery via agentic tree search
finding: Tree-search version without human templates. Three fully AI-written papers went to an ICLR workshop; one scored 6.33 (6, 6, 7), above the average human acceptance threshold, the other two did not. The accepted paper was withdrawn by prior arrangement.
numbers: 1 of 3 manuscripts reached acceptance level; mean 6.33 of 10 (about top 45%).
limits: Workshop bar is low; selection of what to submit was by the authors; the accepted paper reported a mostly negative result.
agent_relevance: Tree search over experiments adds systematic search, but yield was 1 in 3.

source: Cornelio et al. (2023) Combining data and theory for derivable scientific discovery with AI-Descartes
finding: Pairs symbolic regression with logical reasoning over background axioms. Recovers Kepler's third law, relativistic time dilation and Langmuir adsorption from few data points by rejecting candidates that cannot be derived from theory.
numbers: Three law case studies (Nature Communications paper, PMC10097814); no aggregate rate read.
limits: Needs hand-written axioms; few laws tested.
agent_relevance: Fit alone cannot tell equally good formulas apart; use background theory as a second filter (derivability).

source: Bjurstrom et al. (2026) Investigating uncharacterised genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae using robot scientists
finding: Robot Scientist Eve tested hypotheses about the uncharacterised gene YGR067C. Some predicted effects held (lower respiratory transcripts) but others were not significant.
numbers: About 880 of ~6000 yeast ORFs still uncharacterised. Some pathway genes had positive log2 fold change but missed FDR significance; NADH/NAD+ ratio did not shift in the mutant.
limits: One gene, one lab; simulation-based higher-order predictions only partly supported.
agent_relevance: Hypotheses from models get partial support; log which predictions failed.

source: King et al. (2009) The automation of science (robot scientist Adam), repository abstract page
finding: Adam generated and tested yeast functional genomics hypotheses with lab automation; conclusions were confirmed by separate manual experiments. Only the Warwick repository abstract was read; full paper not read, so opened is false.
numbers: Over 10,000 research units in a nested structure 10 levels deep; 6.6 million biomass measurements. Counts of hypotheses and confirmations not obtained.
limits: Abstract page only; full text restricted.
agent_relevance: A closed loop of hypothesis, experiment, record works when the domain is a formal knowledge base.

source: Williams et al. (2015) Cheaper faster drug development validated by repositioning of drugs against neglected tropical diseases (Eve), press summaries only
finding: Eve screened yeast carrying malaria parasite DHFR vs human DHFR and flagged TNP-470 as a candidate. A skeptic doubts the efficiency claims. Seen only through press summaries; paper itself blocked (403).
numbers: Screening over 10,000 compounds per day; TNP-470 stopped resistant P. vivax DHFR yeast at about 1000 times lower concentration than human DHFR yeast (press report, not verified).
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Lead only; do not cite numbers until the paper is read.

source: Langley (1981) Data-driven discovery of physical laws (BACON.4)
finding: Original BACON paper could not be opened (403 from publisher). Only a secondhand description was read in Cranmer 2023: Bacon used heuristic strategies for brute-force search over expression trees and found simple physics laws from idealized data.
numbers: No BACON-specific numbers obtained.
limits: Source blocked; web search quota ran out before an open copy was found.
agent_relevance: Need an open copy before citing exact BACON rediscovery counts or its heuristic list.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) LLM-SRBench, memorisation check (second line)
finding: On 100 original Feynman problems, LLM methods show sharp drops in numeric error and much lower symbolic error than on the disguised LLM-SRBench sets. This pattern points to recall of known equations, not stepwise discovery.
numbers: Figure 1 of the paper compares Llama-3.1-8B on Feynman vs LSR-Transform and LSR-Synth; direct prompting gets 2-7% SA on Transform.
limits: Memorisation shown by curve shape, not by a training-data audit.
agent_relevance: Textbook-law tests overstate discovery; disguise variables in our own tests.

source: Si et al. (2024) idea diversity finding (second line)
finding: Scaling up idea generation gives few new ideas: after deduplication at cosine 0.8, about 5% of generated seed ideas remain. LLM self-evaluation as reviewer was not reliable versus humans.
numbers: Dedup threshold 0.8 with all-MiniLM-L6-v2; about 5% non-duplicate.
limits: Single embedding model; NLP topics.
agent_relevance: Best-of-N sampling for hypotheses needs a dedup step and an outside judge.

source: Luo et al. (2025) label-noise test of data leakage and metrics (second line)
finding: Their controlled data-noise setups show how benchmark gains can be misread: with 30% shape-flip noise one reported accuracy figure fell from 95.31% to about 71.5% and with 30% color-flip noise to about 66.5% in the noisy-label setting.
numbers: 95.31% clean vs 71.51% (30% shape-flip) vs 66.48% (30% color-flip); one column group of the table read from the PDF text.
limits: Table layout is garbled in the text extract; read as indicative.
agent_relevance: Check metrics for the right split and noise before claiming a gain.

source: Chen et al. (2024) ScienceAgentBench, compute versus cost (second line)
finding: More inference compute raised success from about 32-34% to 42.2% (o1-preview) but at more than ten times the cost of other models.
numbers: 42.2% vs 34.3% best other; cost ratio above 10x.
limits: Single benchmark of 102 tasks.
agent_relevance: Budget rules: spend extra compute on test-and-repair, not on longer drafts.

source: Cross-benchmark synthesis from b03, b06, b05 (reading note, not a new study)
finding: Exact-equation recovery, numeric fit and out-of-domain error are different outcomes. AIFeynman tops SRBench at zero noise but not with noise; LLM methods drop sharply when recall is blocked (LLM-SRBench); LLM-SR gains are largest out of domain.
numbers: AIFeynman 53% exact (zero noise, SRBench); best LLM method 31.5% symbolic accuracy (LLM-SRBench); LLM-SR E. coli OOD NMSE about 0.0037 vs above 1.
limits: Different problem sets, so numbers are not comparable across papers.
agent_relevance: Score our agent on three things: exact match, fit, extrapolation.
